### WebGPU
Part 1 of 2

WebGPU supports graphics and compute workloads in compatible secure contexts. Adapter availability depends on browser, operating system, and device policy; it is not a system GPU-utilization monitor.

### WebAssembly
Part 2 of 2

WebAssembly is a compact code format designed for portable execution. In a browser it operates within sandbox and API constraints; it does not grant unrestricted system access.

### DNS
Part 1 of 2

DNS translates domain names into network addresses. A DNS error can come from a typo, a local resolver, or the domain’s configuration.

### Cookies
Part 2 of 2

Cookies are small values attached to requests under browser rules. Sites use them for sessions and preferences; third parties can use them for tracking. Deleting session cookies commonly signs you out.

### Cache-Control
Part 1 of 2

Cache-Control defines caching rules. No-cache permits storage but requires validation; no-store asks caches not to store the response. They are not interchangeable.

### HTTP 304
Part 2 of 2

A 304 response tells a client its cached representation is still valid for a conditional request. It is normally part of successful caching, not a missing page.

### IndexedDB
Part 1 of 2

IndexedDB is an asynchronous, transactional browser database. Cole uses it for conversations. Browser storage is local to the origin and profile, and users or the browser can remove it.

### Local storage
Part 2 of 2

localStorage holds string key-value data for an origin and is synchronous. It can be cleared by the user and may be unavailable or restricted. It is not an appropriate place for secrets that must be hidden from site scripts.

### Backups
Part 1 of 2

A backup is an independent recoverable copy, not merely another folder on the same failing device. Sync can propagate deletion, so version history and offline copies matter.

### Browser synchronization
Part 2 of 2

Browser sync may send selected bookmarks, passwords, tabs, or settings to the account provider. It is separate from Cole’s local storage.

### Mozilla Firefox
Part 1 of 2

Firefox uses Gecko rather than Chromium’s Blink. Enhanced Tracking Protection reduces some cross-site tracking. Site compatibility and extension behavior can differ from Chromium browsers.

### Apple Safari
Part 2 of 2

Safari uses WebKit and integrates with Apple’s operating systems. Updates generally arrive through system updates. Some web APIs and extension formats differ from Chromium.

### WebGL
Part 1 of 2

WebGL provides GPU-accelerated graphics through a browser-managed context. Contexts may be lost because of resource pressure, resets, or policy.

### WebGPU
Part 2 of 2

WebGPU supports graphics and compute workloads in compatible secure contexts. Adapter availability depends on browser, operating system, and device policy; it is not a system GPU-utilization monitor.

### Service workers
Part 1 of 2

A service worker can intercept requests within its scope and provide cached resources offline. It has a separate lifecycle and cannot directly access the DOM.

### Back-forward cache
Part 2 of 2

The back-forward cache can preserve a page for fast history navigation. It differs from the HTTP cache and is subject to eligibility and eviction.
